messages.content:
A person asked this in the Slack thread of an incident Argus is responding to:

what has Argus done about this so far?

This is everything Argus has recorded about the incident, oldest first:

- 2026-10-27T23:49:02Z Argus: Received HighErrorRate on io-shop
- 2026-10-27T23:49:02Z Argus: Moved the incident to INVESTIGATING - a worker took the incident up
- 2026-10-27T23:49:02Z Argus: Called in the Investigator Agent
- 2026-10-27T23:49:03Z Investigator Agent: Asked for the service's per-minute metrics, anchored on 23:49
- 2026-10-27T23:49:04Z Investigator Agent: Read back 361 minutes of metrics
- 2026-10-27T23:49:04Z Investigator Agent: Placed the start of the incident at 23:43
- 2026-10-27T23:49:04Z Investigator Agent: Recorded where the 3 replicas run - all on Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB
- 2026-10-27T23:49:04Z Investigator Agent: Asked for production change events - deploys, releases and flag changes on the service, the 1 day before Oct 27 23:43
- 2026-10-27T23:49:04Z Investigator Agent: Read back 1 production change
- 2026-10-27T23:49:04Z Investigator Agent: Read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 replicas run one revision, which the history does not name
- 2026-10-27T23:49:04Z Investigator Agent: Asked for the service's log lines, the 36 minutes before 23:49
- 2026-10-27T23:49:04Z Investigator Agent: Read back 128 log lines
- 2026-10-27T23:49:04Z Investigator Agent: Formed 1 candidate cause, best first: The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at 23:43. That enabled a code path that raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, and the account page error rate rose from about 1% to about 33%. No deployment landed, the rollout is converged, and latency and resources are flat.
- 2026-10-27T23:49:04Z Investigator Agent: Read every channel available
- 2026-10-27T23:49:04Z Argus: Read the flag provider's history - 1 flag change by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 23:49:04
- 2026-10-27T23:49:05Z Argus: Moved the incident to MITIGATING to act on the leading candidate
- 2026-10-27T23:49:05Z Argus: Called in the Mitigation Agent
- 2026-10-27T23:49:06Z Mitigation Agent: Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature, moved from ON to OFF
- 2026-10-27T23:49:08Z Mitigation Agent: Waiting to see whether the service is still at the incident's level, from 23:50 - up to 120s
- 2026-10-27T23:49:08Z Mitigation Agent: Looked at the service - still at the incident's level
- 2026-10-27T23:51:03Z Mitigation Agent: Looked at the service - no longer at the incident's level since 23:49
- 2026-10-27T23:51:03Z Mitigation Agent: Judged the action CONFIRMED
- 2026-10-27T23:51:03Z Argus: Moved the incident to MITIGATED - set flag [monthly-spend-feature] OFF and the rule that fired stopped firing
- 2026-10-27T23:51:11Z Code-Fix Agent: Proposed a fix as a draft pull request - https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/370
- 2026-10-27T23:51:11Z Argus: Filed what was tried on this incident: putting monthly-spend-feature back
- 2026-10-27T23:51:12Z Postmortem Agent: Wrote the postmortem - The service broke at 23:43 UTC and was back to normal at 23:50 UTC, 7 minutes later. 26.2% of requests failed while it was broken, against 1.0% before it began. At its worst, 36.0% failed. The shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by 4,006.73 USD, beyond how much those hours vary on their own. Turning on a new monthly spending summary made account pages fail, most likely because the summary divides by the number of things a shopper bought this month, and for shoppers who bought before but not this month that number is zero. What Argus did: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature (can be put back) - confirmed, still in place. Argus opened a draft fix, PR #370, for a person to review and merge. The faulty calculation was still in the code behind monthly-spend-feature, so switching that flag back on would most likely make account pages fail again for shoppers with no purchases this month.
- 2026-10-27T23:51:29Z A person: Wrote in the incident's thread: what has Argus done about this so far?

Answer only from these lines. Where they do not hold the answer, say that the record does not say, rather than guessing. Do not say Argus will do anything; answer what happened.
Tell what a line says was measured or seen in that line's own words, never as another measure: a service no longer at the incident's level has left that level, which is not the same as being back to normal.

Call submit_answer with your answer.

tools.description: Submit your answer to the person's question about the incident.

answer.description: The answer, as it will be posted in the thread: a few plain sentences, addressed to the person who asked.
